text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty -> page fired: GPU_MEM_PRESSURE pool=prod-gpu-pool region=us-west-2 severity=high
PagerDuty: Alert -> Incident #INC-2026-4321 (assigned: Anika H.)
Anika H.: acked :white_check_mark: I'm on it, triaging now.
Anika H.: quick snapshot from node gpu-node-17:
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
Attached GPUs : 1
GPU 0 Memory Usage : 15360 MiB / 16384 MiB
Processes:
  python (pid 23456) consuming 12.8GB
  python (pid 23478) consuming 10.2GB
```
Anika H.: kernel logs show repeated cuda alloc failures and OOM prints, e.g.:
```
[ 1203.456789] NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x46:0xffffffff)
[ 1203.456800] nvidia-mmu: MMU context create failed: -12
[ 1203.457000] cuda: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
```
Marta S.: tagging in infra: @infra-bot can you check pool autoscaler + recent deploys?
infra-bot: autoscaler metrics for prod-gpu-pool: provisioned=12 desired=12 pending=0, recent scale events=0 in last 10m
Ravi P.: sounds like fragmentation or a runaway job; any noisy customers?
Anika H.: initial customer impact: elevated 5xxs and latency on transformer-infer route, ~4% error rate over last 5m, top affected orgs: AcmeCorp, BrightApps (small subset of requests returning 503s).
Dave L.: routing fallback kicked in for some requests to cpu-safe variants. We saw an increase in cost but reduced failure blast radius.
Anika H.: immediate mitigation plan:
- identify heavy PIDs and kill long-running staging jobs off GPU-node-17 (short term)
- cordon & drain node if leaking memory across processes
- trigger node reboot if drains fail
- temporarily route new requests off prod-gpu-pool to spare-pool-usw
- engage infra for kernel/NVIDIA driver traces and NVML errors

Anika H.: running `ps aux | grep python` on node, will try to kill pid 23456 now.
Marta S.: please use `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` when ready, coordinate with SRE to avoid evicting high-priority jobs.
Anika H.: killed pid 23456, freeing ~12.8GB. Memory usage dropping.
Anika H.: issuing cordon/drain now:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```
Incident Bot: Eviction events detected: 8 pods evicted, 2 pods failed to reschedule due to affinity constraints.
Ravi P.: rerouting in flight: updating router rule to prefer spare-pool-usw for transformer-infer, policy TTL 5m.
DevEx (Dave L.): posting customer-facing note draft to #support: "We detected degraded performance for a subset of GPU-backed inference requests; automatic fallbacks were enabled and we are mitigating. We'll update in 30m."
Anika H.: after drain, node memory now shows 3.2GB used / 16GB, no OOMs seen in kernel logs for last 2m.
PagerDuty: Incident escalated to SRE lead (Marta S.) due to sustained high severity.
Marta S.: I'm running a diagnostic script across pool to look for fragmentation patterns and stale CUDA contexts.
Marta S.: diag snippet:
```
for node in $(nodes); do ssh $node 'python -c "import pynvml; pynvml.nvmlInit(); print(pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo(pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(0)))"'; done
```
Marta S.: found one node with repeated cuda contexts not being released post-kill, raising a kernel-level suspicion. Filing infra ticket: INF-2026-778.
infra-bot: created ticket INF-2026-778: Investigate NVML memory context leak on kernel 5.15.0-88.
Ravi P.: what's ETA for node replacement or reboot? We should prefer reboot if kernel resources are stuck.
Anika H.: coordinating with infra: requesting soft-reboot of gpu-node-17 in 5m if post-drain checks pass.
Anika H.: sanity check metrics: error rate decreased to 0.9% in last 2m, tail latency for transformer-infer P95 down from 1.8s to 0.6s.
Marta S.: can we mark incident as contained? Impact limited, automatic fallbacks mitigated most customer errors. I propose "contained" but keep monitoring and keep incident open until infra ticket closed.
Anika H.: agreed. I'll update incident status: Partial degradation -> Contained. Notifying oncall replacement.
Ravi P.: handing off to night oncall @Ravi P. (me) at 21:00 PT. Summary I'll paste in handoff message in 10m.
Anika H.: handoff notes: root cause suspected: NVML/CUDA memory context leak after certain workloads; mitigation: killed runaway processes, drained node, reboot queued; fallback routing applied to spare pool; INF ticket created for kernel/driver investigation; customers were routed to CPU-safe variants for affected requests minimizing errors.
Anika H.: Slack action: please react with :thumbsup: once you've read and accept handoff.
Ravi P.: :thumbsup: taking over. I'll follow up with infra team on reboot progress and watch for repeated OOM alerts.
Dave L.: created a short runbook snippet for this class of issue in docs: link: https://internal.redwood/infrarunbooks/gpu-oom-quickplay (will add more diagnostics).
Anika H.: posting final metrics snapshot to incident ticket and closing PagerDuty alert after handoff.
PagerDuty: Alert -> acknowledged by Anika H. Escalation cleared.
Incident Bot: note: auto-pager suppression enabled for this alert class for 15m to avoid noisy repeats while we stabilize.
Ravi P.: follow-ups: schedule a controlled disrupt window to reboot questionable nodes tomorrow 02:00 PT; notify customer success for any high-touch customers; postmortem required if INF ticket identifies driver bug.
Marta S.: adding owners for postmortem: Marta S., Ravi P., Infra Eng.
Anika H.: thanks team, closing thread. :heart:
